'''Raul''' "'''Raulzinho'''" '''Togni Neto'''  ({{IPA|pt-BR|ʁaˈuw toɲɲi ˈnɛtu|lang}}; born 19 May 1992) is a Brazilian professional [[basketball]] player for [[San Pablo Burgos]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]]. He is also a member of the senior men's [[Brazilian national basketball team]]. Neto also holds an Italian passport.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eurohopes Basketball Prospects - News - Raulzinho to EH: ''I wanted to go to NCAA, but I was a pro in Brazil and I couldn't''|url=http://www.eurohopes.com/news/5600/raulzinho_to_eh_i_wanted_to_go_to_ncaa,_but_i_was_a_pro_in_brazil_and_i_couldnt|website=EuroHopes.com|language=en|access-date=October 14, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Neto was drafted by the Atlanta Hawks with the 47th pick in the 2013 NBA draft. He was then immediately traded to the Utah Jazz.

=== Minas Tênis Clube (2008–2011) ===
Neto made his professional debut in 2008 with [[Minas Tênis Clube (basketball)|Minas Tênis Clube]] during the [[2008–09 FIBA Americas League]]. He played a further three seasons for [[Minas Tênis Clube|Minas]] and even represented the World Team at the 2010 [[Nike Hoop Summit]].

=== Gipuzkoa (2011–2014) ===
After averaging 12.6 points and 2.2 assists per game as a sixth man for Minas in [[2010–11 NBB season|2010–11]], Neto signed with [[San Sebastián Gipuzkoa BC|Lagun Aro GBC]] of Spain for the 2011–12 season. After averaging 8.5 points and 2.9 assists per game during the 2012–13 season with [[Gipuzkoa Basket|Lagun Aro GBC]], Neto was selected with the 47th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He was later traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] on draft night.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-acquires-draft-rights-raul-neto-atlanta|title=Jazz Acquires Draft Rights to Raul Neto from Atlanta|work=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2013|access-date=June 27, 2013}}</ref> However, he did not join the Jazz and instead returned to [[Gipuzkoa Basket|Lagun Aro GBC]] for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13822|title=Raul Neto will not yet join Utah Jazz|work=InsideHoops.com|date=July 18, 2013|access-date=July 18, 2013}}</ref>

=== Murcia (2014–2015) ===
On August 1, 2014, Neto signed a three-year deal with [[CB Murcia|UCAM Murcia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/129835/raul-neto-inks-with-ucam-murcia.html|title=Raul Neto inks with UCAM Murcia|work=Sportando.com|date=August 1, 2014|access-date=August 1, 2014}}</ref> He parted ways with the club following the 2014–15 season in order to sign in the NBA.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/167644/the-jazz-will-sign-raul-neto.html|title=The Jazz will sign Raul Neto?|work=Sportando.com|date=July 8, 2015|access-date=July 8, 2015}}</ref>

=== Utah Jazz (2015–2019) ===
On July 9, 2015, Neto signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Lea|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-guard-raul-neto|title=Jazz Sign Raul Neto to Multi-Year Contract|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2015|access-date=July 9, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Jazz in the team's season opener against the [[Detroit Pistons]] on October 28, 2015, recording 8 points and 3 assists as a starter in a 92–87 loss.<ref>{{cite web|first=Noah|last=Trister|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/UTADET/gameinfo.html|title=Pistons top Jazz 92-87, improve to 2-0 on season|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015}}</ref> On January 27, 2016, Neto was selected to the [[2016 NBA All-Star Game|2016]] [[Rising Stars Challenge]] as a member of the World Team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/rodney-hood-and-raul-neto-named-2016-bbva-compass-rising-stars-challenge|title=Rodney Hood and Raul Neto Named to 2016 BBVA Compass Rising Stars Challenge|work=NBA.com|date=January 27, 2016|access-date=February 2, 2016}}</ref> On February 19, 2016, he scored a season-high 15 points in a 111–93 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Kareem|last=Copeland|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/BOSUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Favors scores 23 as Jazz beat Celtics 111-93|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2016|access-date=February 21, 2016}}</ref> On January 9, 2017, he spent a day with the [[Salt Lake City Stars]], Utah's [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-assign-alec-burks-dante-exum-and-raul-neto-salt-lake-city-stars|title=Jazz Assign Alec Burks, Danté Exum and Raul Neto to Salt Lake City Stars|work=NBA.com|date=January 9, 2017|access-date=January 9, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-recall-alec-burks-dante-exum-and-raul-neto-salt-lake-city-stars|title=Jazz Recall Alec Burks, Danté Exum and Raul Neto from Salt Lake City Stars|work=NBA.com|date=January 9, 2017|access-date=January 9, 2017}}</ref> He was reassigned to Salt Lake City on January 11, 2017,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-assign-alec-burks-and-raul-neto-salt-lake-city-stars|title=Jazz Assign Alec Burks and Raul Neto to Salt Lake City Stars|work=NBA.com|date=January 11, 2017|access-date=January 11, 2017}}</ref> and then recalled the next day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-recall-alec-burks-and-raul-neto-salt-lake-city-stars|title=Jazz Recall Alec Burks and Raul Neto from Salt Lake City Stars|work=NBA.com|date=January 12, 2017|access-date=January 12, 2017}}</ref> He played 9 of 11 matches of the Jazz during the [[2017 NBA Playoffs|playoffs]]. On July 6, 2018, Neto re-signed with the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jazz Agree to Terms with Favors, Exum and Neto|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-agree-terms-favors-exum-and-neto|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 9, 2018|date=July 6, 2018}}</ref> On July 2, 2019, Neto was waived by the Jazz due to the [[Mike Conley Jr.|Mike Conley]] trade with Grizzlies.

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2019–2020) ===
On July 4, 2019, Neto agreed to sign with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: 76ers signing Raul Neto as backup point guard|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/report-76ers-signing-raul-neto-040332665.html|access-date= July 4, 2019|date = July 4, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Team Signs Neto|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-signs-neto|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 12, 2019|date=July 12, 2019}}</ref>

=== Washington Wizards (2020–2022) ===
On November 22, 2020, Neto signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-neto-retain-mathews|title=Wizards sign Neto, retain Mathews|work=NBA.com|date=November 22, 2020}}</ref> As a member of the 2020-2021 Wizards, Neto appeared in 5 playoff games and started in 3.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Raul Neto Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/n/netora01.html |access-date=2022-05-01 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Cleveland Cavaliers (2022–2023) ===
On July 8, 2022, Neto signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on a one-year, $2,463,490 contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Ricky Rubio, Robin Lopez, and Raul Neto|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-rubio-lopez-neto-signings-220708|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2022|access-date=July 8, 2022}}</ref>

On August 5, 2023, Neto signed a one-year deal with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe Beko]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raul Neto Fenerbahçe Beko'da|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2023/8/raul-neto-fenerbahce-beko-da|website=Fenerbahce.org|date=August 5, 2023|access-date=August 5, 2023|language=Turkish}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Fenerbahce inks ex-NBA guard Raul Neto|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/fenerbahce-inks-ex-nba-guard-raul-neto/|website=EuroLeagueBasketball.net|date=August 5, 2023|access-date=August 5, 2023}}</ref> However, he never played for the team, because on August 26 he suffered a knee injury playing for the [[Brazilian national basketball team]] in the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], which kept him out of action for almost a year. On July 8, 2024, during an interview, Neto revealed that Fenerbahçe terminated his contract after the injury and never officially communicated their decision.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Raul Neto reveals Fenerbahce cut his contract last year, hopes to play in Olympics|url=https://basketnews.com/news-208879-raul-neto-reveals-fenerbahce-cut-his-contract-last-year-hopes-to-play-in-olympics.html|date=2024-07-08 |access-date=2024-09-05 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Esporte Clube Pinheiros São Paulo (2024)===
On October 15, 2024, Neto returned to Brazil as he signed a contract with [[Esporte Clube Pinheiros (basketball)|Pinheiros Basquete]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Raul Neto returns to Brazil, pens a contract with Pinheiros |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1728397/raul-neto-signs-with-pinheiros-brazil/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=15 October 2024 |language=en |date=15 October 2024}}</ref>

===FC Barcelona (2024–2025)===
Neto was announced as a new [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] player on November 24, 2024, signing a contract for the remainder of the season. The Barcelona board chose Neto after the season-ending injury suffered by [[point guard]] [[Nicolás Laprovíttola]] had left a vacant spot in the roster.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raul Neto joins FC Barcelona basketball team |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/4175432/raul-neto-joins-fc-barcelona-basketball-team |website=FC Barcelona |access-date=26 November 2024 |language=en |date=24 November 2024}}</ref> On December 1, 2024, the club announced Neto would be out for four weeks due to an [[Adductor muscles of the hip|adductor]] injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Barca new signing Raul Neto out four weeks |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1750393/barca-new-signing-raul-neto-out-four-weeks/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=5 December 2024 |language=en |date=1 December 2024}}</ref> Neto's contract with Barcelona would be terminated in January 2025 after a mutual agreement between the club and the player. The agreement took place after Neto suffered another injury to his left hamstring, making his stay at Barcelona barely over a month long and only making 2 appearances for the Catalans.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raul Neto leaves Barça |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/4192923/raul-neto-leaves-barca |website=FC Barcelona |access-date=2 January 2025 |language=en |date=2 January 2025}}</ref>

===San Pablo Burgos (2025–present)===
On July 3, 2025, Neto was announced as a new player by [[San Pablo Burgos]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Raul Neto, experiencia para la dirección de juego burgalesa
 |url=https://www.sanpabloburgos.com/es/noticia/ver/17334-raul-neto-experiencia-para-la-direccion-de-juego-burgalesa.html |website=sanpabloburgos.com |access-date=3 July 2025 |language=es |date=3 July 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
Neto gained attention after leading the Brazil under-18 team to an impressive runners-up showing at the 2010 [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/FIBA-Americas-U-18-Championships-Top-International-Prospects-3528/|title=FIBA Americas U-18 Championships: Top International Prospects|work=DraftExpress.com|date=July 1, 2010|access-date=July 1, 2010|archive-date=15 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121015195705/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/FIBA-Americas-U-18-Championships-Top-International-Prospects-3528/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He followed that up by being the youngest member of the senior [[Brazil national basketball team]] during the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], but played sparingly. He later participated for the senior national team at the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]], the [[2013 FIBA AmeriCup]], and the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. During the World Cup, he had a strong performance against Argentina in the round of 16, when he scored 21 points to lead Brazil to a win.<ref>{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Lea|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/raul-neto-scores-21-beat-argentina|title=Raul Neto Scores 21 to Beat Argentina|work=NBA.com|date=September 8, 2014|access-date=September 8, 2014}}</ref> Neto also played at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20181123112048/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/Raulzinho%20Neto/pid//_//players.html Raulzinho  NETO (BRA).]</ref>
